stem: An 18-month-old boy who has not received routine vaccines has had fever, irritability and vomiting for 2 days. He is lethargic with a stiff neck and a bulging fontanelle. A lumbar puncture shows a high opening pressure.
oneliner: 18M + unvaccinated + fever, vomiting, stiff neck, bulging fontanelle + high opening pressure → which CSF profile?
ask: Which cerebrospinal fluid profile is most likely?

options.A: Lymphocytes predominate, protein mildly raised, glucose normal
options.B: Lymphocytes predominate, protein very high, glucose low
options.C: No cells, protein high, glucose normal
options.D: Neutrophils predominate, protein high, glucose low

whyNot.A: The **viral** pattern; an unvaccinated toddler this ill with high pressure points to bacteria
whyNot.B: The pattern of **TB or fungal** meningitis, which evolves over **weeks**, not 2 days
whyNot.C: **Albuminocytologic dissociation** of Guillain-Barré; this boy has meningeal signs, not weakness
whyNot.E: He has **meningitis signs and high pressure**; a normal CSF would not explain them

answer: Neutrophilic pleocytosis, raised protein and low glucose (bacterial meningitis)
why: Bacteria in the subarachnoid space attract **neutrophils** and break down the blood-CSF barrier, so **protein rises**. Bacteria and neutrophils **consume glucose**, so CSF glucose falls (below about 40% of serum). Opening pressure is **high**. Viral meningitis gives **lymphocytes with normal glucose**.

idea.rule: Bacterial = neutrophils, high protein, low glucose; viral = lymphocytes, normal glucose.
also: TB and fungal meningitis: lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose
Guillain-Barré: high protein with normal cell count
Likely organisms in the unvaccinated young child: S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae type b
Neonates: group B Streptococcus, E. coli, Listeria
